To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the performance of auto-vectorization of codes with complex data dependencies is comparable to manually vectorized codes; (ii) the performance of codes that do not fit the traditional vectorization model, such as those with complex control flow, is also comparable to manually vectorization; (iii) this is enabled by a new architecture that exposes more flexibility to the compiler; (iv) this architecture can also be used to accelerate legacy codes that were not written to exploit data parallelism; and

(1) exposing the accelerator to the compiler enables auto-acceleration performance comparable to manually optimized implementations and (2) this is achieved by making the accelerator's microarchitecture more flexible.

the performance of a compiler can be greatly enhanced by making the microarchitecture of an accelerator more flexible, exposing this flexibility to the programmer, and then using the compiler to automatically generate code that exploits this flexibility.
